ghs.en: Taichi: "And anyway, doesn't Touko wear the same clothes every day now?"
ghs.assessment: Taichi says that Touko too used to wear the same clothes every day. The English puts her action in the present and adds 'now.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "And anyway, doesn't Touko wear the same clothes every day now?"

rows.jp: 「アレは同じ服を何着も持ってるから……」

ghs.en: Youko: "But 'that' owns a number of identical clothes..."

rows.jp: ふらふらと、霧が出てきた。
rows.en: Kiri emerged, unsteady on her feet.

ghs.en: Kiri came out, staggering on her feet.

rows.en: She looked at me as if I were her enemy.

ghs.en: A look in her eyes as if seeing an enemy.
Kiri: "How dare you, how dare you!"

rows.jp: 悲しみの涙ではなかった。
rows.en: Those were not tears of sorrow.

ghs.en: Those were not tears of sorrow.

rows.jp: 虐げられ、奪われ、玩弄された者だけが持ち得る感情。
rows.en: Only someone oppressed, robbed, and toyed with could feel that emotion.

ghs.en: This was an emotion that only those who have been persecuted, dispossessed and toyed with can feel.

rows.jp: 「やっぱり……あなたは……あなたたちは……」
rows.en: “I knew it... You... Both of you...”

ghs.en: Kiri: "I knew it... you... you people are..."

rows.jp: 曜子ちゃんが、刃物を取り出した。

ghs.en: Youko-chan took out an edged weapon.

rows.jp: 「……憎しみにとらわれていて、太一にとって危険だもの」
rows.en: “...Hatred has consumed her. She is dangerous to you.”

ghs.en: Youko: "...she is a prisoner of hatred, she is something dangerous to Taichi."
ghs.assessment: Youko says that Kiri is dangerous to Taichi. 'She is something dangerous' is ungrammatical and needlessly dehumanizing.

highlights.text: Youko: "...she is a prisoner of hatred, she is something dangerous to Taichi."

ghs.assessment: なにをいまさら dismisses the objection as too late now. 'Why even at this point' is an incomplete question.

highlights.text: Kiri: "Why even at this point."

rows.jp: 「……どうせ……生きていても、あなたの食い物にされるだけじゃないですか！」
rows.en: “...Even if I live, you’ll only use me for your own gratification!”

ghs.en: Kiri: "...whatever happens... as long as I live, will I not just be made into food for you!"

rows.jp: 「どう言い訳していいものかわからないけど……」
rows.en: “I don’t know how I can possibly excuse myself, but...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I have no I idea how I could possibly explain this, but..."
ghs.assessment: The English contains the duplicated phrase 'no I idea.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "I have no I idea how I could possibly explain this, but..."

rows.jp: 応援団なみの謝りっぷりだと自画自賛。
rows.en: I congratulated myself on an apology worthy of a cheer squad.

ghs.en: A quality of apology on par with a cheering squad, if I may boast.
ghs.assessment: Taichi praises his own apology as being delivered like a cheering squad. 'A quality of apology' is an unnatural nominal calque.

highlights.text: A quality of apology on par with a cheering squad, if I may boast.

rows.jp: 霧は一瞬ぽかんとしていた。が、すぐ屈辱に歪む。
rows.en: Kiri stared blankly for an instant. Then humiliation twisted her face.

ghs.en: Kiri went slackjawed for one instant. But, soon, that warped into humiliation.

rows.jp: 「なんですか、それ……なんなんですか、あなたは？」

ghs.en: Kiri: "Just what was that... what, just what are you?"
ghs.assessment: Kiri asks what the just-delivered apology is. 'What was that' incorrectly shifts the immediate question into past tense.

highlights.text: Kiri: "Just what was that... what, just what are you?"

rows.jp: 「理解できない、理解できないですっ！」
rows.en: “I don’t understand! I don’t understand you!”

ghs.en: Kiri: "I cannot understand, I just CANNOT understand!"
Kiri: "...but... I do not care anymore..."

rows.jp: 乱れた胸元を抱えて、歩み去る。
rows.en: Clutching her disheveled blouse shut, she walked away.

ghs.en: Holding down the disheveled pit of her stomach, she walks away.
ghs.assessment: 胸元 is her disheveled chest, neckline, or front of her clothes. 'Pit of her stomach' identifies a different body area.

highlights.text: Holding down the disheveled pit of her stomach, she walks away.

ghs.assessment: 黙殺 means that Kiri completely ignores him. 'Killer silence' is a literal wordplay invention and does not state the deliberate ignoring.

highlights.text: Killer silence.

ghs.en: Youko: "...Taichi... got completely absorbed in that."
ghs.assessment: Youko directly tells Taichi that he got too carried away. The English refers to him in third person and adds 'in that' as an external summary.

highlights.text: Youko: "...Taichi... got completely absorbed in that."

rows.jp: 追いかけようとすると、背後から声がかかった。
rows.en: I was about to go after Kiri when Youko spoke behind me.

ghs.en: As I go to follow her, I am called from behind.
ghs.assessment: Taichi tries or starts to pursue Kiri when a voice stops him. 'As I go to follow her' treats the pursuit as already underway.

highlights.text: As I go to follow her, I am called from behind.

rows.jp: 「いいじゃないか。どうせ繰り返されるんだ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Not a problem, is it? This'll all be done over again anyway."

rows.jp: 「俺の固有の時間なんて、無意味なものだろ」
rows.en: “My own unique time doesn't mean anything.”

rows.jp: 「日記の情報量を増やすためにも、いろいろするべきだ」
rows.en: “I should try everything I can, if only to add more information to the diary.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "And for the sake of increasing the amount of information in the diaries, I ought do all kind of things."
ghs.assessment: The phrase requires 'all kinds of things,' not singular 'all kind of things.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "And for the sake of increasing the amount of information in the diaries, I ought do all kind of things."

rows.jp: 「それだけで動いているなら確かに……けど太一のは違う」
rows.en: “If that were truly all that drove you, perhaps. But it isn't.”

ghs.en: Youko: "If this happened just because of that certainly... but Taichi is wrong here."
ghs.assessment: Youko says that if increasing the diary's information is Taichi's sole motive, his claim would be valid, but his actual motive is different. The English instead says an event happened for that reason and that Taichi himself is wrong.

highlights.text: Youko: "If this happened just because of that certainly... but Taichi is wrong here."

rows.jp: 「太一は、壊れた玩具を大切にしすぎる」
rows.en: “You care too much for broken toys.”

ghs.en: Youko: "Taichi is treating a broken toy with far too much care."

rows.jp: 「死ぬまで、君とだけ向かいあって暮らせとでも？」
rows.en: “Do you expect me to spend the rest of my life facing no one but you?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "You say I should be living opposite of you alone, until death?"
ghs.assessment: Taichi asks whether he is supposed to live facing only Youko until death. 'Living opposite of you alone' suggests opposition or a house across from hers and misplaces 'only.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "You say I should be living opposite of you alone, until death?"

ghs.en: Taichi: "...never making connections with anybody else."
Taichi: "Inside a tiny circle of friends, forever..."
ghs.assessment: The source says only 'inside a small circle.' Adding 'of friends' fixes the circle's membership without support.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Inside a tiny circle of friends, forever..."

rows.jp: 「１００人の家族と暮らすのと、私と暮らすのに、大きな違いがあるわけじゃない」
rows.en: “There is no essential difference between living with a family of one hundred and living with me.”

ghs.en: Youko: "Living within a family of a hundred people and living with me alone are things of no great difference."

rows.jp: 「太一の判断基準は、普通を意識しすぎてると思う」
rows.en: “I think your idea of what is normal matters far too much to you.”

ghs.en: Youko: "In Taichi's evaluation criteria there's too much attention paid to the ordinary, I think."

rows.jp: 「自分に必要なものは、自分の分析から来るものなのに」
rows.en: “But what you need should come from understanding yourself.”

ghs.en: Youko: "But what the self needs is something that comes from the analysis of the self."
Taichi: "...what's wrong with the normal now."
ghs.assessment: Taichi asks what is wrong with being normal. 'What's wrong with the normal now' is ungrammatical and treats normality as a definite object.

highlights.text: Taichi: "...what's wrong with the normal now."

rows.jp: 「彼女たちは、一時の玩具にしかならないのに」
rows.en: “Those girls will only ever be temporary toys.”

ghs.en: Youko: "For those girls cannot possibly become more than temporary playthings."
ghs.assessment: The declarative sentence is incorrectly introduced by the dangling conjunction 'For.'

highlights.text: Youko: "For those girls cannot possibly become more than temporary playthings."

rows.en: “...They won't last. It'll be over almost at once.”

ghs.en: Youko: "...it won't last. It will end soon."

rows.jp: 「太一自身が、終わらせてしまいたくなる」
rows.en: “You'll be the one who wants to end it.”

ghs.en: Youko: "Taichi himself will want to make it all end."

rows.en: Just as I had a moment ago.

ghs.en: Just like it was long ago.
ghs.assessment: さっき means just now or a moment ago. 'Long ago' places the comparison in the distant past.

highlights.text: Just like it was long ago.

rows.jp: 彼女の言いたいことは、わかる。

ghs.en: I understand what she wants to say.

rows.jp: 「今週は好きにさせてもらうよ」
rows.en: “This week, I'll do what I want.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Let me do whatever I like this week."
ghs.assessment: Taichi asserts that he will do as he likes this week. 'Let me do' changes the declaration into a request for permission.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Let me do whatever I like this week."

rows.jp: 「もう今日は帰っていいから」

ghs.en: Taichi: "You should just go home for the day."
ghs.assessment: Taichi says that Youko may go home now, dismissing her. 'Should go home' changes permission or dismissal into advice or obligation.

highlights.text: Taichi: "You should just go home for the day."

rows.jp: 「そんな追い返そうとしなくても……」
rows.en: “You don’t have to try so hard to send me away...”

ghs.en: Youko: "Don't just push me away so much..."

rows.jp: 「見守ってくれなくていいって言ってるんだよ。だって、たとえ危険だったとしても明日は日曜だ。ご破算の日だよ？　無茶したって構わないでしょ？」
rows.en: “I’m telling you I don’t need you watching over me. Even if I am in danger, tomorrow is Sunday—the day everything is wiped clean. What does it matter if I take risks?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I'm saying you don't need to watch over me. Because, even if there was some danger, tomorrow's Sunday. Ain't that the day of the clean slate? If I do something stupid it won't be that much of a problem, right?"

rows.jp: 「今のあなたが固有の時間を生きているように、私もまた、固有の時間を生きてる」
rows.en: “Just as the person you are now is living his own unique time, I am living my own unique time too.”

ghs.en: Youko: "You, as you are now, live in eigentime and I, myself, am living in eigentime."

rows.jp: 「今のあなたと対になっているのは今の私だけ。当然のことだけれど……」
rows.en: “Only who I am now is paired with who you are now. It should be obvious, but...”

ghs.en: Youko: "Who you are now only forms a pair with me as I am now. That's obvious, however..."

rows.jp: 「固有の私の願望は、次週のそれとは別物で」
rows.en: “What this particular me wants is different from what next week's me will want.”

ghs.en: Youko: "The desire of my eigenself is... going to be different next week."
ghs.assessment: Her present individual desire is a different thing from next week's. 'Is going to be different next week' makes one continuing desire change over time, and 'eigenself' is unsupported jargon.

highlights.text: Youko: "The desire of my eigenself is... going to be different next week."

rows.en: The words came out as a plea.

ghs.assessment: 滅びる means that each weekly self perishes or ceases to exist. Passive 'are destroyed' introduces an outside destructive agent.

highlights.text: Youko: "Every week we are destroyed."

ghs.en: Youko: "Our proprietary is destroyed. In other words,"
ghs.assessment: 個別の滅び means individual extinction or each person's perishing. 'Our proprietary is destroyed' mistakes an adjective about individuality for commercial ownership and is ungrammatical.

highlights.text: Youko: "Our proprietary is destroyed. In other words,"

rows.jp: 「毎週、別の私たちということ……」

ghs.en: Youko: "it means that every week we are different people..."

rows.en: She'd arrived at the same thought I had.

rows.jp: 「他の週にいる私がどうなろうと、知ったことではないけれど……」
rows.en: “I don't care what happens to any other week's me, but...”

ghs.en: Youko: "What the myselves that live in other weeks will do is something that I do not know, however..."
ghs.assessment: 知ったことではない means that she does not care what happens to versions of herself in other weeks. The English instead says that she does not know what they will do.

highlights.text: Youko: "What the myselves that live in other weeks will do is something that I do not know, however..."

rows.jp: 「いろんな可能性の中に、太一が私に優しくしてくれることは……あるの？」
rows.en: “Of all those possibilities... is there one where you're kind to me?”

ghs.en: Youko: "Within all of these many possibilities, does one where Taichi treats me kindly... even exist?"

rows.jp: 「ノートには、そんなパターンはなかった」
rows.en: “No such pattern appeared in the notebook.”

ghs.en: Youko: "In the notebooks there was no pattern like that."

rows.jp: 「……望むものを得ることなく霧散するばかり」
rows.en: “...I just vanish, over and over, without getting what I want.”

ghs.en: Youko: "...there is only vanishing in the mists without obtaining what was desired."

rows.jp: 「私は欠けたまま、消えるだけ」

ghs.en: Youko: "I will just vanish, still incomplete."

ghs.assessment: This will be goodbye. 'Become farewell' is a literal and unnatural predicate.

highlights.text: Youko: "This will become... farewell."

rows.jp: 「ごめんなさい……もう邪魔しない……」

ghs.en: Youko: "Apologies... I will not intrude anymore."

ghs.assessment: 踵を返す is to turn on one's heel. 'Turns away' omits the abrupt physical motion.

highlights.text: She turns away.

rows.jp: 「でも、これだけは記録しておいて」

rows.en: She spoke with her back turned.

ghs.assessment: She speaks with her back turned, not literally 'from her back.'

highlights.text: She speaks from her back.

rows.jp: 「……どこに行っても、あなたを理解してくれる人なんて……いない」
rows.en: “...No matter where you go, you will never find anyone who understands you.”

ghs.en: Youko: "...wherever you go... a person that will understand you... you will never find."

rows.jp: 言葉は重い石となって、胃に落ち込んだ。
rows.en: The words became a heavy stone that sank into my stomach.

ghs.en: Words that are heavy as stones, that drop straight down to the stomach.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese is one past-tense metaphor in which the words become a heavy stone and sink into his stomach. The English uses two malformed present-tense relative fragments.

highlights.text: Words that are heavy as stones, that drop straight down to the stomach.

rows.jp: 廊下を歩む姿が、芥子粒大になって消えるまで、見送った。
rows.en: I watched her walk down the corridor until she dwindled to a poppy seed and disappeared.

ghs.en: I watched until the image of her walking down the corridor turned the size of an ant and vanished.

rows.jp: 決して嫌いなんじゃない。
rows.en: It was not that I hated her.

ghs.en: I don't hate her, I really don't.

rows.jp: だけど……彼女の願望には、矛盾がありすぎる。
rows.en: But... her desires contained too many contradictions.

ghs.en: However... in her wish there are too many contradictions.

rows.jp: 二人の線が交錯することは、ないように思えた。
rows.en: It seemed our two lines would never cross.

ghs.en: The lines of these two people seemed like they would never know mixing.
ghs.assessment: It seemed that the two people's lines would never intersect. 'Would never know mixing' is ungrammatical and changes a geometric crossing into generic mixture.

highlights.text: The lines of these two people seemed like they would never know mixing.
